messages:
isaac: Heads-up — trying to get the new FP8 / AWQ / GPTQ bakeoff qprofiles into Optimize. Need packaging + naming consensus before we push to the registry.

rachael: Quick Q — what are the minimal manifest fields the runtime needs to pick the right profile?

isaac: Proposed minimal set: model_name, model_arch, quant_scheme, bitwidth, seq_len_hint, perf_metrics (p50_ms, throughput), compatibility_tags, checksum, schema_version, artifact_list

simon: Also add consumer hints: recommended_routing_policy, fallback_variant, perf_tradeoff (one of ["latency","cost","quality"]) — Optimize can use that for suggestions.

zane: Strong +1. We must include accuracy deltas vs fp32 per eval suite (or test cohort). If we don't surface deltas QE will block deployments.

olivia: Suggest adding eval_cohorts array: each entry {name, dataset, delta_ppl, delta_acc, top_k_metrics}. That keeps things structured for the UI.

dev-bot: ci: qprofile lint OK (iso/qprof-2143601111) :white_check_mark:

isaac: example manifest snippet below (for discussion):
```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "profile_id": "llama2-13b-awq-std-v1.0.0",
  "model_name": "llama2-13b",
  "model_arch": "decoder-only",
  "quant_scheme": "AWQ",
  "bitwidth": "8",
  "seq_len_hint": 2048,
  "perf_metrics": {"p50_ms": 42.7, "throughput_tokens_s": 3800},
  "perf_tradeoff": "latency",
  "compatibility_tags": ["redwood-optimize-v1", "runtime-2.3+"],
  "eval_cohorts": [
    {"name": "chatty-qa", "dataset": "redwood-chat-qa-v3", "delta_ppl": 0.02, "delta_acc": -0.7},
    {"name": "summarize", "dataset": "redwood-summ-v2", "delta_ppl": 0.01, "delta_rouge_l": -0.4}
  ],
  "artifact_list": [
    {"path": "qweights.bin", "sha256": "<hex>"},
    {"path": "qmeta.json", "sha256": "<hex>"}
  ],
  "package": "llama2-13b-awq-std-v1.0.0.tar.gz",
  "top_level_checksum": "sha256:<hex>",
  "notes": "Canary with 10% traffic. Fallback to fp32 if delta_acc < -1.5 on any core cohort."
}
```

rachael: For naming/versions: do we want to use semver or a specialized qprofile version? My vote: semver for the profile content (major bump for incompatible schema changes). Also keep a human-friendly id like <model>-<quant>-<tag>-v<semver>.

simon: Agreed — add both fields: profile_id (human id) and profile_version (semver). Keep schema_version separate. That lets Optimize check compatibility easily.

olivia: Runtime compatibility rules to encode: minimum runtime that supports the quant scheme + bitwidth and kernel flags (e.g., fp8-support, packed-keys). Maybe add boolean flags like requires_kv_cache_adjustment.

zane: Packaging format: tar.gz containing qmeta.json (the manifest), qweights.bin(s), readme.md, and a small eval_report.csv. Each file SHA256'd and the package signed. Registry validates signature and checks top_level_checksum.

isaac: Rollout policies: Optimize should suggest a canary plan based on eval deltas and perf_tradeoff. e.g., if delta_acc < 0.3% and latency improvement > 20% => suggest 20% canary then 100% over 48h. If delta_acc > 1.0% then recommend manual gating.

rachael: I'll add a UI hook: show perf_tradeoff slider + a small "risk estimate" derived from eval_cohorts. Also show recommended fallback_variant (e.g., fp32 or a different qprofile).

simon: Naming convention proposal (single line): <model>-<quant>-<profile_tag>-v<semver>. Example: `llama2-13b-awq-std-v1.0.0`. Keep profile_tag short: std | conserv | perf | bleeding.

dev-bot: deploy: registry upload queued for iso/qprof-2143601111.tar.gz — ETA ~2m

isaac: One last ops note: add a small field `canary_metrics_watchlist` listing metrics to monitor (ppl, latency_p95, err_rate, hallucination_rate). If any exceed thresholds, auto-roll back.

zane: For QE: checklist = lint -> local runtime smoke -> integrated eval_cohorts run -> package sign -> upload -> small canary -> monitor for 72h. I'll create a GH checklist.

isaac: Great. I'll draft a short RFC capturing the manifest spec, packaging format, naming rules, and the Optimize UI/rollout mapping. Will ping security for signing process. Thanks everyone :rocket:
